html:
The Atakapa were an Indigenous people of the Gulf of Mexico coast, in what is now southwest Louisiana and southeast Texas. They spoke the Atakapa language, a linguistic isolate with no known relatives.

They lived in several bands along the coastal marshes, prairies and bayous, fishing, gathering shellfish and hunting. Their neighbours were the Chitimacha to the east, the Karankawa to the southwest and the Caddo to the north.

From the 1700s they traded with French Louisiana and then the Spanish. Disease and the loss of land to settlers shrank their numbers. Their last recognized chief, Ló, died in 1850. After that the survivors mostly joined the Caddo, the Koasati and other neighbours, though a few kept Atakapa ways into the 20th century.
